reviews.comment:
I don't see what could make his class any worse than the best. His lectures were great and you can tell he cares. He often ties the things we are learning with his research so you know that what you learn isn't all going to waste. Hit the point home in my head that A&M is no joke. 

PREPARE FOR CALORIMETRY

Had Folden in Fall 23. A very solid 4/5 prof for me. His lectures were very thorough and he'd always record them and put them on canvas for anyone who needs them. He'd always have a line of students with questions after class but he'd always take the time to help them out. The only issue I have is that his hw format is somewhat frustrating at times

Professor Folden is the best lecturer I had my first semester. If you are like me and did not take AP Chem in high school this class is definitely not easy. He broke down topics well, answered questions asked with enthusiasm, and kept the lectures within the scope of the material. Folden is definitely the best professor if you are taking Chem 107.

Dr. Folden had strong lectures and was very skilled at simplifying things so they didn't get outside the scope of the class. If you didn't take AP Chem, don't listen to the people saying this class is "easy". My only complaint is other professors might've given more extra credit, but Folden is a good choice who will clearly explain the material.

Prof. Folden is one of the best out there for chem 107
Grade is 40% attendance + hw (free if you don't procrastinate), 20% quiz, and 2x20% exams
Lectures are easy to follow and understand (recorded and can be accessed from zoom), helpful outside of class.
Quiz and exams are easy if you focus in class, do the homework, and go to the SI sessions.

Dr. Folden was a very great lecturer. If you read the textbook and take notes during lecture like he said in the beginning of class an A is almost guaranteed. He is also very receptive to questions and wants you to understand the material.

One of the most rewarding classes I have taken. You must go to lecture because he posts PowerPoints but nothing else. Tests are very fair. We toured the cyclotron and nuclear reactor which I will never get to do again. Labs were fun too. We had 8 people in the class which made the class feel closer together.

107 is a hard class, but Dr. Folden was a great teacher. Easy to understand, and very upfront about what we needed to know and what we didn't. Quizzes and exams were online and asynchronous. Very strict on grading (no extra credit, no curves) but from my understanding that's how every 107 prof was. Highly recommend taking him.

He's a really good professor. He goes over the content really thoroughly during the duration of the class and works through the hard examples. Pay attention during class and you'll breeze through Chem 107

Professor Folden was a very good lecturer and explained the material very well. He was very accessible outside of class and explained the important ideas very clearly, making sure you understood them. He was overall just very solid as a professor and lecturer.

Take this professor. His grading is very simple and  40% of your grade is an easy 100. He is very accessible by email and is very interested in the material he teaches. He explains the material perfectly and his lectures are extremely helpful.

Pretty good, his final being the same questions as the quizzes really saved me since I bombed most of the quizzes. His lectures were pretty entertaining but I didn't feel like they covered quiz material that well, but overall he was good and nice and he is very knowledgeable and speaks clearly so its easy to understand.
Chem is rly hard, but he does a great job of explaining everything. Only thing is that he doesn't round up. Still highly recommend.
Very good professor!

Professor Folden is amazing. He cares a lot about his students, but you still have to work hard to get a good grade. He deals with questions very well and makes sure you understand. It is clear that questions do not bother him, but that he wants his students to learn chemistry. He is super smart and easy to talk to.
Good professor. Lectures, homework, and supplemental instruction are all you need. Easy class, just study.

Folden is a good professor. His lectures are very helpful because they make things easier to understand. He really knows what he's talking about and can give helpful advice on all questions you may have. Class was a little disorganized grade wise, and he didn't give extra credit or bonuses in some areas that other professors did.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This professor is very fast paced and you have no material to study from outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Folden was a good lecturer but gave ZERO resources to study. As long as you attend lectures and write down EVERYTHING he writes and says you should do okay in the class. 

My main complaint is the lack of resources as we didn't have any past exams, no practice questions. 

I found the homework to be very tedious and the quizzes were hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is pretty hard but Professor Folden was a great teacher. You have to go to lectures to understand what's going on. There's weekly homework and it can get pretty tedious. He gives quizzes once every three weeks and those are pretty hard. However if you go to class, pay attention, and study for the quizzes/exams, you can still get an A
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Folden is clearly passionate about chemistry. 107 is a VERY fast paced course, however, so be prepared. Very generous with bonuses on top of the iClicker and homework grades. He was always open to answering questions outside of class and knows his stuff.

Dr. Folden is really passionate about what he teaches and he tries to inspire his students with science. The lectures can be pretty stuffed at times, so looking at the textbook before hand helped me keep up.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very solid professor. Good lectures and tests/quizzes were extremely doable. Most of the complaints on here seem to be from students who have not made the transition from high school to college yet. You do have to put in effort into studying to do well, but as long as you pay attention during lectures and do the studying, it's an easy A.

I invested $200 into A+ tutoring for this course because his lectures and teaching style confused me. No curve to any exams or quizzes. No extra credit opportunities. He added 10% to homework and 30% to clicker questions. At the end of the semester, I had a 69.47% and he didn't round.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: How to pass this class.1)Folden does not provide many resources outside lectures, so re-watch lectures and absorb his teaching.2)Get ahold of Dr.Hilty's TA videos;they provide an excellent summary and go over things you might have missed in the lecture.3) Don't go over homework on how to solve the problem; conceptually understand what is going on.

Prof Folden is a great guy. I can tell he really loves chemistry. However, most of the material in the quizzes and final exam is from outside knowledge whether it be a different chem course or the textbook. Sometimes the quizzes barely touch on the topics discussed in class and the questions are generally worded confusingly.

Folden gives fairly easy clicker questions and great lectures. He is always on track or ahead of schedule. Makes deadlines clear in syllabus - however no canvas notifications for hmwk. He posts all the lectures online but doesn't upload full slides (but they're in the lecture videos). Very enthusiastic and nearly fooled me into enjoying chemistry!

Very great professor. Came in with background knowledge of AP Chemistry but Professor Folden does a great job in explaining the material that I did not remember. The class is inherently difficult due to the nature of chemistry, so make time to practice. Doesn't offer extra credit so study hard for the quizzes and exams. Helpful and friendly.

Professor Folden is a good guy; I just don't think he should be teaching first year chem. It was very much you were expected to know how to do it. He did very few practice problems in class and the I got a tutor and would have q dropped if I didn't. If you took AP chem in hs then you might like him but if you hate chemistry don't take him.

His lecture is great and I learned a lot from that. Some people may complain that he has quizzes every other week that is not similar to the HW. But I'm pretty sure other CHEM 107 professors do that as well. Else, it would be too easy. The quizzes and exams are completely doable to get an A on as long as you study and understand the concepts.

Dr. Folden is an awesome professor for this course. His lectures are very helpful and he offers lots of ways to make sure you get an A through iClicker and Homework. The quizzes and exams in this class are pretty difficult but he covers a lot of things in lecture to help out. This course sucks overall but Dr. Folden does make it a little easier.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's very smart and doesn't get off task much in his lectures, although sometimes he gets behind (the homework will show you how to do what might not get covered). However, in his lectures, he writes his notes as he speaks so he's easy to follow. Overall, I would recommend him.

Good professor, really cares about chemistry and will take time to explain things well. However, the material in lectures lags behind homework/quiz material, so you will spend a lot of time teaching yourself how to actually solve problems. If you haven't taken AP Chemistry it will be quite a struggle.

He spends time in class to teach stuff we don't need to know, and then his quizzes look nothing like the homework or what we go over in class, so even if you study for them you have a 50/50 shot of whether you recognize the question. His homework is a good grade boost, but once again is not super useful because the questions don't matter for quiz.

Professor Folden is an amazing teacher who clearly has a very complex understanding of the material. He is really nice, and cares about the success of his students. The lectures get a tad boring, but only because he wants to make sure everyone thoroughly understands each concept. Lots of HW, but it's easy. Definitely take him if you get the chance!

He is a really good prof!! It's a tough class but I think that he does a good job explaining and answering questions. He's very nice and responsive, and records all lectures (does use clickers though). He does bi-weekly quizzes that are a little hard, but if you study you should be fine. He gives average amount of HW.

Dr. Folden is an overall good professor and you can really see that he knows what he is talking about. He cares about his students' understanding, which is reflected in his lectures. There is homework due every Sunday, and biweekly quizzes which do require studying. Use your quizzes for exam study material!

Prof Folden is awesome. He puts a lot of effort into his lectures and it really helps for his students to understand the information. All of them are recorded too so if you miss class you can just watch online. Lots of easy points for HW and in-class participation too. Get him for Chem if you can I promise you wont regret it.

Folden is genuinely a genius and is super knowledgeable of chemistry. However, tamu chemistry, especially for engineers, is extremely difficult. He made it as easy as it could be and really cared about his student. Answered questions and paused every now and then so we could catch up on notes. He gets some hate just because the curriculum is hard.

This class is a lot of work and the quizzes are the worst part. I study for 2 hours before each one with the practice assignments from OWL and the quizzes still look nothing like them or my notes. He also regularly ignores questions.
Folden is pretty good just focus on the quizzes, and even then he drops the lowest one. Also his tests are pretty much a repeat of the quizzes before hand and he is a great teacher. Highly recommend.

He does really make you work for your grade. You're going to have to put in effort to get the grade you want. Although there are easier professors I think you actually end up learning the material well. He doesn't give mock exams so his exams are pretty difficult but overall I think he does a good job teaching all of the material.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Please be wary of all of these green ratings. I used this rating to choose my professor and it really is a mistake. The people who rated are likely really good students who were able to teach themselves. Professor Folden is a little more harsh than other professors.

Dr. Folden is good as a person. However, unless you are amazing at Chemistry already or know how to teach yourself, dont take it. He doesnt believe in extra credit or any mock exams so theres already no help there. And whenever you have a question in class he just says sorry we dont have time. Take Bethel or McCartney if you can.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took AP chem. He seems kinda mean at the beginning but he's nice after a while. He curves the end grade and has some retakes but he won't tell you so you don't rely on it. He doesn't believe in practice tests/ review sheets which really sucks. Go to the SI or you will be unprepared for the test. I didn't like the order he taught concepts.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily difficult. He's really fast paced and his tests don't even compare to the material gone over in lecture's or in the textbook. Take any other chem professor because I basically taught myself with youtube vids
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As a person, love the dude. As a professor, eh.. he's alright. But in comparison to other chem119 profs, TAKE FOLDEN!!! also, GO TO THE SI SESSIONS!!! He curves ALOT and allows for retests.

Dr. Folden is a great professor teaching a fast- paced subject. In Chem 119, he allowed us to retake the mini-exam and the first exam and that helped my grade out immensely! You must do Aleks and try to get a 100%! Study and show up to class and you can get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall Prof Folden was good and the best option out of the 119 profs. Personally, his tests were hard (go to SI). At times he can be rude and ignore your questions but was good at explaining concepts. He let us retake exam 1 and mini-exam. ALEKS is time-consuming, but lab, homework, in-class questions saved my grade. 88% was an A for his class!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Folden is a really good professor. Material is hard but he explains them very well.
Great professor, but tough tests. I studied super hard and followed his advice, but still did bad on them. The other attributes really help in this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Folden is a great guy-you can tell he wants students to understand the topics & doesn't hesitate to answer any questions. He expects you to work hard & won't deal with any bs. He tries to avoid teaching off powerpoints which is nice. Tests are challenging, but if you study/go to SI's then you're set. ALEKS can be annoying, but what homework isn't?

Switching to Folden was the best choice I have made. Really tries to explain to where students understand. Very helpful office hours and SI's. I had to work VERY hard for this class (but i was awful at chem in high school). Start ALEKS atleast 3 days early. Very lecture based exams. Dont think you can cram the day before for exams, you cant.

He gives extra credit through in class participation. He writes notes as he teaches which is better than just reading from the slides. SI helped a lot with practice problems for his tests. His tests are about 20 questions so you can't get too many wrong if you want the A but ALEKS, Clicker questions, and lab will help your grade.

Folden was overall a good professor. I found chemistry to be very difficult and had to put in a lot of time outside of class, so the long homework assignments did not help much. Read the textbook before class, it helps clear up the material. He gave us participation credit in class and let us retake an exam that had a low average. Not a bad choice.

Dr. Folden is a great professor. It's clear that he works very hard for his students. This class is hard and that should be expected since it is chemistry. The ALEKS homework is quite tedious but if you need help he will make sure to answer everyone's question. Overall, very loveable character.

I hate chemistry with all my heart, HOWEVER, prof Folden made it very enjoyable. He makes us laugh and he teaches well. He posts his recorded lectures online as well as his lecture slides. Pay attention and take good notes. I had his class all online, but he tried his best to make it work for us. Love this guy, would take again!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took AP Chem in high school and barely scraped a 3 on the AP exam, but I felt really confident in his class. He cares very much for his students and puts in extra effort to ensure that we could have our questions answered during class. Out of all of my teachers, I feel he was the most prepared for teaching during a pandemic in an online setting.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very passionate of what he teaches. He does not post the majority of his notes online, So attendance is even more important than usual. His lectures are usually very good, making attendance less of a chore than usual.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Folden is an okay professor. He explains things well in lecture and is open to questions. He isnt very accessible outside of class. The concepts tested on his exams arent very difficult, but his tests are mostly multiple choice and only 11 questions and the individual questions count for so many points with no partial credit.

Professor Folden is the BEST. I'm not saying he is the easiest professor to take, but you can tell through his lectures that he truly cares about his students and loves the subject that he teaches. Even though his lectures aren't technically mandatory, you should still go because a lot of test material comes from the lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Folden is great. Attendance is not mandatory, but he has clicker questions that counts towards your grade. I would recommend going to each of his classes cause he normally does practice problems that could possibly be on the test. If you write down everything that he writes and says and read the book before class, and study notes, will get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Folden is a real gem, he is articulate, funny and nerdy. I really enjoyed his class. The only problem i had (and this could not be of his doing) was that his test were extreamly short and if you missed a single question you could lose 8 to 10 points. That made it really difficult to bring your grade up in this class. Ps most were MC

Dr. Folden is awesome, both as a professor and as a human being. He's the only nuclear chemist on campus, so he's very knowledgeable and eager to share it with students. My only complaint is that there is not enough time to finish tests for a MWF class, so just be warned that even though the material is doable, it's the timetable that will get you.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Folden is really passionate about chemistry so learning the material isnt as dreadful. Also lectures with a very clear and loud voice.

Go to class and write down everything he writes. 3 exams and a comprehensive final, so study your notes for each one well in advance! Exams are a mixture of multiple choice and free response, but you must show all your work on free response for full credit. The homework is not bad, just around 15-20 problems per chapter. Overall, great professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite professor at A&M so far. He really breaks things down so that everyone can understand the material. He can be very funny and is beyond helpful in his office hours. The work load is not too much and very manageable. His exams are definitely do-able but you still have to really work for that A.

Folden's class is pretty easy if you go to lecture and pay attention. He does use clickers for a part of the overall grade, so attendance is encouraged. Folden is easy to understand and explains things in a way that makes them simple to comprehend. The exams do have harder content than the in-class examples, so make sure to do the homework.

Class isn't mandatory, but he does have clicker questions worth a small part of your grade. He's a really good professor, and happy to answer questions during class. He's known to make minor errors in some problems, but he always corrects them. Tests aren't impossible, mainly related to problems he works through in class.

He's extremely helpful, but uses OWL's for the homework. I think Satan probably writes those questions, because I've never had such difficult homework for any class in college. I'm already bad at chemistry, and OWL's frustrated me so much that it was almost impossible to pass that class. Be prepared for a challenge.

Dr. Folden is an outstanding professor. His lectures were very clear, he was enthusiastic and genuinely cared about his students. Also, he offered a review before every test and gave hints during lectures to questions that could be on the test. Still have to work hard, but worth the effort.

I can't say how awesome Prof. Folden was!He is a great at giving lectures. He tries to make his points very clear and tries his best to make you understand in the easiest way possible. He genuinely cares for his students and on occasion he can be pretty hilarious. You can also tell he loves what he does. Take him!

I loved Dr. Folden! He broke down the material so it was very easy to comprehend. He also goes slow enough during lecture so your hand won't cramp. He takes his time explaining the topics -  even if that means his a little behind for the next lecture. His tests are straight forward, and he even holds review sessions (yes, for the final too).

He's really helpful, and his lectures are very on topic and clear. Whenever he's asked a question, he always repeats the question so that everybody knows what question he's answering to. Highly recommend this professor... would like him as my organic chem professor!
Awesome professor. Clear communicator and very helpful.

He writes out his notes during the lecture so you don't miss any important points. He also holds review sessions before his tests so you know what all will be on the test. Never overloaded us on OWL homework. He breaks chemistry down even for people that dont remember much from chem101.
Class is difficult due to subject material. Prof is a good lecturer. Allows one page of notes on each test.
